# Task 037 shared UCI schema-version String conformance corpus.
#
# ONE canonical corpus drives the Rust, C++, and Ada generated validators, so
# the three backends are proven to agree rather than each passing its own
# curated subset. Rust-side tests read this file and emit the cases into the
# probe program for every language.
#
# FORMAT
#   '#' begins a comment line; blank lines are ignored.
#   VALID   <input> => <expected stored form>
#   INVALID <input>
# <input> is a C-style escaped string so whitespace cases are unambiguous;
# only \s (space), \t, \n, \r, and \\ are used.
#
# AUTHORITY
# The profile is read verbatim from the pinned UCI release bytes:
#   UCI 2.5 093610b7753944059360d3236770ab446d039556
#           UCI_MessageDefinitions_v2_5_0.xsd:145460
#   UCI 2.6 78eb61b6112c8bffa40820c33124b57787fc5bd9
#           UCI_MessageDefinitions_v2_6_0.xsd:145708
# The two releases are byte-identical for this declaration:
#
#   <xs:restriction base="xs:string">
#     <xs:minLength value="7"/>
#     <xs:maxLength value="57"/>
#     <xs:pattern value="[0-9]{3}\.[0-9]{1,2}(\.[0-9]{1,2})([a-z]{1,2})?(_[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{1,45})?"/>
#   </xs:restriction>
#
# STRUCTURE, left to right:
#   [0-9]{3}                  exactly 3 ASCII digits
#   \.                        one literal '.'
#   [0-9]{1,2}                1-2 ASCII digits
#   (\.[0-9]{1,2})            '.' then 1-2 ASCII digits   -- REQUIRED, unquantified
#   ([a-z]{1,2})?             optional 1-2 ASCII lowercase letters
#   (_[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{1,45})?   optional '_' then 1-45 ASCII alnum/'-'
#
# THIS IS NOT NNN.NNN.NNN.NNN. The four-group spelling that appears as this
# declaration's own uci:version attribute is REJECTED by the type it annotates.
# The referencing element's documentation agrees, giving "002.0" and "001.9b".
#
# whiteSpace. xs:string's intrinsic whiteSpace is 'preserve' and is NOT fixed
# (section 4.3.6); this restriction adds no whiteSpace facet. Normalization is
# therefore the identity: every VALID case stores its input UNCHANGED, and no
# whitespace is ever trimmed or collapsed into validity.
#
# Anchoring. Patterns match the ENTIRE literal (section 4.3.4.3), so leading
# and trailing junk are rejected rather than ignored.
#
# Length. minLength/maxLength count CHARACTERS (sections 4.3.1-4.3.3). Every
# character the pattern admits is ASCII, so a byte count equals the character
# count for every accepted value. The pattern's own bounds are 7 and 57, which
# coincide exactly with the declared facets; both are still enforced.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- valid cases

# Minimum-length value: 3+1+1+1+1 = 7 characters, exactly minLength.
VALID 000.0.0 => 000.0.0
# The Sleet interoperability baseline version, as used by the public tutorial.
VALID 002.5.0 => 002.5.0
# An ordinary release with two-digit middle and last groups.
VALID 002.50.10 => 002.50.10
# Maximum digits in every numeric group.
VALID 999.99.99 => 999.99.99
# Optional one-letter suffix: the "001.9b" shape named in the element docs.
VALID 001.9.0b => 001.9.0b
# Optional two-letter suffix, the widest the {1,2} quantifier allows.
VALID 001.9.0zz => 001.9.0zz
# Optional underscore tail, minimum width (1 character after '_').
VALID 002.5.0_a => 002.5.0_a
# Underscore tail exercising the full alnum + '-' alphabet.
VALID 002.5.0_Release-2A => 002.5.0_Release-2A
# Both optional groups present together.
VALID 002.5.0ab_build-7 => 002.5.0ab_build-7
# Maximum-length value: 3+1+2+3+2+46 = 57 characters, exactly maxLength.
VALID 999.99.99zz_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa => 999.99.99zz_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa

# -------------------------------------------------------------- invalid cases

# Empty string: below minLength and matches no pattern branch.
INVALID
# The conventional four-group spelling. This is the single most important
# negative case: it is what the type's own uci:version attribute looks like,
# and this very type rejects it. A fourth group has no production.
INVALID 000.001.000.000
# Three-group form with 3-digit components: the middle group allows at most 2.
INVALID 002.500.100
# The required third group is missing entirely. Length 5 also fails minLength.
INVALID 002.5
# First group too short: [0-9]{3} is exact, not a minimum.
INVALID 02.5.0
# First group too long.
INVALID 0002.5.0
# Middle group too long.
INVALID 002.500.0
# Last group too long.
INVALID 002.5.000
# Missing separator between first and second group.
INVALID 0025.0
# Extra separator producing an empty group.
INVALID 002..5.0
# Trailing separator with no following digits.
INVALID 002.5.0.
# Wrong separator: ',' is in no character class.
INVALID 002,5,0
# Wrong separator: '-' is only legal inside the underscore tail.
INVALID 002-5-0
# Alphabetic character where a digit is required.
INVALID 00a.5.0
# Uppercase suffix: the suffix class is [a-z], lowercase only.
INVALID 002.5.0B
# Three-letter suffix exceeds the {1,2} quantifier.
INVALID 002.5.0abc
# Underscore tail present but empty; {1,45} requires at least one character.
INVALID 002.5.0_
# Underscore tail one character past its 45-character limit. The whole value is
# 58 characters, so this also exceeds maxLength.
INVALID 999.99.99zz_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
# Underscore tail containing a character outside [a-zA-Z0-9-].
INVALID 002.5.0_bad+tail
# A second underscore tail; the group is unquantified and occurs at most once.
INVALID 002.5.0_a_b
# Leading whitespace. whiteSpace is 'preserve', so this is NOT trimmed into
# validity -- it is rejected, because ' ' is in no character class.
INVALID \s002.5.0
# Trailing whitespace, rejected for the same reason.
INVALID 002.5.0\s
# Interior whitespace.
INVALID 002.5\s.0
# Tab control character.
INVALID \t002.5.0
# Line feed, including the trailing-newline shape a careless reader would strip.
INVALID 002.5.0\n
# Carriage return.
INVALID 002.5.0\r
# Leading junk. Patterns are anchored, so a valid substring does not suffice.
INVALID v002.5.0
# Trailing junk, likewise.
INVALID 002.5.0-SNAPSHOT
# A valid value embedded in surrounding text.
INVALID version=002.5.0
# Non-ASCII input. No character class admits a character above U+007F, so this
# is rejected before any length comparison, which is what keeps the byte-count
# implementation of a character-count facet sound.
INVALID 002.5.0é
# Non-ASCII digit lookalike: ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT TWO is not in [0-9].
INVALID ٢٠٢.5.0
